_about: Every choice in the piece lives here. tools/build_piece.py reads the 'build', 'choose', 'time' and 'pitch' sections; the player (stage 2) reads the same file. Keys starting with _ are notes, ignored by the code.

build._sitting_gap: seconds of silence in both logs together that end a sitting
build._default_duration: seconds given to a tool call whose PostToolUse never came
build._max_tool_duration: a PostToolUse later than this after its PreToolUse is not its pair
build._agent_apps: PAULA: check. Apps that count as being with the agents; leaving them is a departure, coming back a return. Your focus log has Code (VS Code) 162 times, Claude 60, Terminal 15.
build._min_tool_calls: a session's stretch needs this many tool calls to go in the pool

choose._about: Which three stretches of real work are laid over each other and played as if simultaneous. 'auto' takes the busiest stretch of each of the three busiest sessions; or list stretch ids from data/pool.json, in voice order.

light._about: Where the window switching (the light) comes from.
light._source: own: each agent brings the switching from its own time. stretch: the stretch below is laid over the whole piece instead, independent of the agents.
light._stretch: a stretch of focus.jsonl, local time. The default is the hour on slide 13: 69 window switches, of which 47 leave or come back to the agent apps.
light._live_fallback: for --last-minutes: if no switching was logged in the window (the focus logger not running), use the stretch above instead

time._about: How real seconds become played seconds.
time._mode: compressed: fit the piece into 'target' seconds. realtime: play 'excerpt' seconds from 'offset' at 1:1.
time._gap_cap: in compressed mode, an idle stretch longer than this many real seconds is shortened to it first, so hours of waiting do not become silence
time._entries: played second at which each voice comes in; each voice is then fitted into the time left after its entry
time._tail: seconds kept free at the end of a compressed piece for the last bells to ring out

pitch._about: Also used for the MIDI file. MIDI note numbers; D minor pentatonic.
pitch._voice_roots: one register per agent, like a consort of viols: bass, tenor, treble
pitch._tool_degrees: degree of the scale a tool sounds on, within its voice's register. 'tick' is a dry percussive tick, not a pitch. Anything unlisted uses 'other_degree'.
pitch._summons_degree: the bell: this many scale steps above the voice's root, so it sits in the voice's own register but above its texture
